faq.contact: Still unsure? Talk to us on <discord>Discord</discord>, <telegram>Telegram</telegram> or <email>hello@tokhive.ai</email>.

vendor.question: How do I know the tokens really come from the official vendor?
vendor.answer: Every request is relayed from inside an AMD SEV-SNP confidential VM that can only open TLS connections to official vendor endpoints. Each response carries a signed attestation report (application measurement, upstream host and response hash) that you can check with our open-source verifier.

credentials.question: Can TokHive or other users see my credentials or prompts?
credentials.answer: Bee encrypts upstream credentials with the TEE public key before uploading them. Hive processes buyer requests for routing and execution, and failure diagnostics can retain request and response content. Providers do not see buyer content through Bee's encrypted relay.

earn.question: How much can I earn as a provider?
earn.answer: Earnings depend on your available quota, provider rates and the requests you successfully serve. Each request is settled individually, and you can review your settled earnings in the dashboard.

usage.question: Will sharing affect my own usage?
usage.answer: Sharing uses your subscription quota. You can stop sharing at any time when you need that quota for your own requests.

prices.question: How are prices set?
prices.answer: Prices are set at a discount to the official vendor prices. The discount is adjusted periodically based on supply and demand.

tools.question: Which tools and SDKs work with TokHive?
tools.answer: Tools that use the OpenAI Responses or Chat Completions API, or the Anthropic Messages API: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Cursor, the official SDKs, LangChain and more. You only change the base URL and the API key. The docs list the supported features.

settlement.question: How do settlement and withdrawals work?
settlement.answer: Earnings are credited to your earnings balance in real time as each successful request settles. Withdraw from your wallet in Web3 stablecoins, with a $10 minimum and a network fee based on the actual on-chain cost. You can review per-request settlement records in your dashboard.

risks.vendor: TokHive is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic or OpenAI. Their terms may not allow sharing a subscription, and a vendor can limit, suspend or close an account that is shared. That risk is yours, and TokHive does not compensate for a lost or restricted subscription.
risks.rejection: If a vendor rejects or rate-limits an account, Hive stops sending it new requests. Requests in progress may fail; failed requests earn nothing, and earnings already settled stay in your balance. TokHive can also pause or ban an account from supply, for example after repeated upstream rejections or a policy violation.

encrypted.description: Bee encrypts upstream access credentials with the TEE public key. Only the TEE can decrypt the uploaded envelope.

settlement.lead: Each successful request credits your earnings balance as it settles. Withdraw from your wallet in Web3 stablecoins, with a $10 minimum withdrawal and a network fee based on the actual on-chain cost.

idle.question: What does "idle quota" mean?
idle.answer: Idle quota is unused capacity in your subscription. You choose when to share it by starting or stopping sharing.

slower.question: Will my own requests ever be slower or blocked?
slower.answer: You can stop sharing at any time.

stop.question: Can I stop at any time?
stop.answer: Yes. Pause sharing from Bee on your computer with the bee pause command, and start again with bee resume. Stopping sharing does not affect earnings already settled.

withdraw.question: When are earnings settled, and how do I withdraw them?
withdraw.answer: Each successful request is settled in real time and credited to your earnings balance. Withdraw from your wallet in Web3 stablecoins, with a $10 minimum and a network fee based on the actual on-chain cost. Settlement does not wait for your balance to reach the withdrawal minimum.

calculated.question: How are earnings calculated?
calculated.answer: For each billing item, such as input, output and cached tokens, your quote is the model's base price multiplied by your quote factor. You can keep the platform default factor or set your own in the Console. Buyers pay your quote, TokHive takes its commission from it, and you earn the rest. Requests go to the lowest available quote first, so a higher factor earns more per token but may serve fewer requests. The calculator above uses illustrative assumptions.

credits.question: Can sharing use my paid ChatGPT credits?
credits.answer: Yes. When an OpenAI account has used up its subscription window but still has paid credits, Hive keeps sending it requests and OpenAI charges those credits. It stops when the credits run out or reach your overage limit. Pause sharing if you do not want your credits used. Claude accounts are not affected.

apiKey.question: Can I also share an OpenAI API key?
apiKey.answer: Yes. Bee can offer an OpenAI Platform API key as fallback supply when subscription accounts are busy. The key is encrypted for the TEE like your subscription credentials. OpenAI bills you for that usage, while you earn your usual quote less the platform commission, which can be less than OpenAI charges you, especially for cache writes and long-context requests that OpenAI prices higher. You set the key's concurrency and can pause it in the Console.

registered.question: Someone has already registered my subscription account. What can I do?
registered.answer: Each subscription account can be shared by only one TokHive account, on a first-come basis. If yours was registered by someone else, contact hello@tokhive.ai. Once we have verified that you control the account, we can release it so you can register it.

computer.question: Do I need to keep my computer on?
computer.answer: Yes. Keep your computer on, connected to the internet and running Bee while sharing. Your computer must stay awake; while it is asleep or offline, it cannot receive new requests.

verify.title: Check any response in one command.

requestId.title: Grab the request ID
requestId.description: Use the X-Request-Id header returned by your TokHive API call.

run.title: Run the verifier
run.description: The verifier checks the AMD SEV-SNP report, AWS NitroTPM evidence and the signing-key binding.

measurement.title: Compare the measurement
measurement.description: The snp-app: identity must match the SHA-256 digest of the expected application bundle.

upstream.title: Check the upstream
upstream.description: The signed upstream host must match the expected vendor endpoint.

verify.instructions: Run make build in the verifier repository first. Set TOKHIVE_API_KEY to your buyer API key, TOKHIVE_REQUEST_ID to your request ID, and TOKHIVE_EXPECTED_APP to the production snp-app:{sha} identity from the signed release catalog below. This example checks Anthropic's upstream host and compares the exact upstream response body saved as response.raw.

release.title: Know which TEE image to expect.
release.lead: Each TEE release and each environment it runs in is recorded in a signed release catalog. Take the expected application identity from that catalog, not from the receipt you are checking, and check the catalog's signature against the key on this page before you trust it.
release.note: This page is the independent channel for the production signing key; staging pre-releases use a different key. Compare it with the release-signing.pub attached to each release; do not trust a key read from the release assets alone. A valid signature shows who published the catalog, not what is running now; the hardware evidence in your receipt shows that.
